Each is worth a factor on its own and neither alone reaches the answer: the height ratio runs from 2.721 at an \ell-equivalent cutoff of 900 to 2.393 at 2400, so a cutoff set at the reported multipole is a systematic and not a rounding .

The comparison is made on the polarisation path, in the configuration the control is calibrated in. The 133-bin unlensed one is where the shape rejection is quoted, and its control sits at 2.10 per bin because the ceiling cuts the damping tail .

Subtracting the driving is what measures it: removing every coupling to the potential moves the control's first peak from 220 to 274 and \ell_{1}/\ell_{A} by 0.1792, so the modes carrying the first peak are driven and the shift is the driving's size .
Run on this arm the same subtraction gives 0.1717---the potential's grip within four per cent of the control's, and slightly weaker rather than stronger .

Both arms integrate that horizon from a\to0, the plasma being handed over at the branch point on this one and the control having no other start, so the comparison does not confound the rate with the start ; and here the two agree, the comb at 298.0 against a reported scale of 302.9.

And the likelihood is run, both arms scored on the same bins by the same code, with the amplitude fitted so that what is compared is shape. The result is still a rejection of this arm's spectrum and is stated as one. On the full-range lensed configuration---\ell=100--1996, 185 bins, the lensing carried by the same derived operator on both arms---the control returns \chi^{2}=214.1, or 1.16 per bin,

That is the unfavourable of the two configurations and it is the one quoted, the same comparison unlensed over 133 bins giving 279.4 against 584.0, a factor 2.09; lensing is worth proportionally more to a spectrum whose peaks are already in place .

The band-by-band comparison is spread across the range --- 2.11, 1.90, 6.70 and 8.74 per bin against the control's 0.77, 1.44, 2.62 and 3.73 over the four quarters from \ell=100 to 1300, read on the unlensed configuration --- so the disagreement is not one feature carrying the whole of it .

The oscillation it raises is itself 1.044 times the control's about its own envelope .

And the three features this arm's residual shows and the control's does not are all \Delta's: the peak-and-trough asymmetry, the \ell\simeq1000 trough where \Delta carries -1.074 of the arm's -1.177 in fifteen bins, and the growth with multipole---which \Delta does monotonically where neither residual does, a residual being \Delta on a noise floor of order one that flattens it .

And the baryon density cannot supply the contrast at any value: its response to \omega_b saturates, spanning 0.028 over the whole range with increments falling monotonically, so four per cent is beyond its reach rather than away from its fitted point .

Nor is it the distance: the two arms' comoving distances to last scattering differ by 0.449 per cent with this arm's the larger, their acoustic angles agreeing to 0.085 per cent, and projecting either arm's own source through the other's distance moves its contrast by under a per cent---in the direction that makes the difference larger rather than smaller .

The intercept of that rise covers one across the same twelve settings, 1.017 with a spread of 0.010, so what is established is the growth with wavenumber and not a constant offset: whatever the projection does differently here, it does nothing at the longest acoustic wavelengths and more of it at each shorter one .

The sound speed the kernel sees is therefore 0.455 on the control and 0.397 here, and a difference in that ratio is term-independent by construction, grows with wavenumber, and vanishes for a window narrower than one acoustic period---which is the signature above .

Read physically the law says one thing: a wider \chi-extent narrows the kernel's acceptance in wavenumber, so less of an acoustic period is averaged over and more of the comb survives; this arm's visibility is the 14.6 per cent wider in \chi while accumulating the same sound horizon to 0.08 per cent, and that is why it retains more .

So the two rates do not compete for the line-of-sight integral; they divide it. The integral \Delta_\ell(k)=\int S\,j_\ell(k(\eta_0-\eta))\,\mathrm d\eta runs over one variable, and that variable is the stacking conformal time because \chi=\eta_0-\eta is a separation read across leaves; the plasma's quantities then enter it as functions of that variable, carried through the Jacobian \mathrm d\eta_

So a sound horizon carried on the leaf rate has no lower endpoint to place and the acoustic angle is an output, exactly as the handover requires; the same quantity carried on the stacking rate would need its start supplied by hand, and the control, whose single rate obeys the leaf law at 0.9985, is why integrating from a\simeq0 was never in question there .

Built instead with the projection's distance on the leaf rate it closes the whole of it: \chi^{2}=186.135, level with the control's own value; sign changes landing on the control's own 87; a longest run of 8, which is the control's exactly .

Where the plasma starts moves the scale and not the peak, which is why the start is not free. Scanning a hand-placed start over a factor of 3.6 runs \ell_{A} from 360.6 down to 239.3 while the first peak sits between 204 and 208 throughout : it moves the denominator of \ell_1/\ell_A and leaves the numerator where it is , so the spacing such a start reports is not the spacing its spectrum carries.

The peak set is the observable the slope is not, and it is read on the same banked spectra. Taking the peak positions against integer index after dividing out one global power law---a de-tilt the same control forces, since without it a primordial tilt appears to move peak positions it cannot move---the common offset and the odd--even alternation separate the baryon direction from a pure tilt by fa

And the two candidate carriers move that pair in opposite senses on both components: on the control the driving gives \Delta\varphi=+0.126 with \Delta\mathrm{alt}=-0.0247 while the baryon direction gives -0.0278 and +0.0108---a difference of sign on two independent components rather than of magnitude on one .

Nor does that reading turn on where the threshold for it was set: taken at the unfavourable end of the interval instead of at its centre, one full unit of the driving is 12.5 standard deviations and the observed point sits at 0.75, so both figures quoted above survive the change .
